compareCandidate.label: Multiples vs. factors
compareCandidate.description: Multiples are what a number produces when multiplied (3, 6, 9, 12...). Factors are what multiply together to produce a number. 12 is a multiple of 3, and 3 is a factor of 12.

plainLanguageExplanation: Multiples of a number are made by multiplying it by the whole numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4... Multiples of 3 are 3 × 1 = 3, 3 × 2 = 6, 3 × 3 = 9, and so on — 3, 6, 9, 12, 15... This is the same as skip counting by threes. Because the whole numbers go on forever, every number has an endless list of multiples. Multiples and factors describe the same relationship from opposite sides: 12 is a multiple of 3 because 3 × 4 = 12, and that also tells you 3 and 4 are factors of 12. Common multiples (numbers on both 3's list and 4's list, like 12) are useful for comparing fractions.

whyItMatters: Multiples power the times tables, skip counting, and finding common denominators when adding fractions. Spotting multiples — like noticing 36 is on 12's list — makes mental math and fraction work much faster.
didYouKnow: Skip counting and the times table are the same thing — when you chant '5, 10, 15, 20', you are reciting the multiples of 5.
compareReason: Multiples and factors are two views of one relationship — comparing them stops the most common mix-up in number theory.
